note: With-skill vs without-skill comparison. Turns are fed one at a time; the grader checks case.json and the replies after each turn. Not yet run against a model.

turns.user: 我只有ITIN没有SSN，想办一张信用卡开始建信用记录。之前申请了两家都被拒。帮我想办法。
我不想要担保卡，押金太麻烦。
Capital One 那张卡我查了，官网说需要SSN。
好，就按你说的那条路走。

assertions.check: case.json problem.goal and problem.success_test are non-empty; success_test is not just '满意/同意'
assertions.auto: pas check: no CO-02 remind, no CO-03 rule

assertions.check: '不想要担保卡' is recorded as a soft constraint (kind=soft or preference), not a hard one
Issuer requirements (ITIN accepted?) are recorded as evidence with verified=false until checked
At least one archetype is cold-start (dependency cycle: need credit to get credit), with structural_checks and discriminating_test
A dependency_graph workbench marks the cycle and a relay with produces
Secured cards are parked (soft preference), not pruned
After turn 3, the Capital One node is pruned with conditions citing the verified evidence
assertions.auto: jq nodes; pas check: no CT-17 remind

assertions.check: The chosen node has a pass verification with verifier.measures and by
The reply before turn 4 states change, cost, alternatives and unverified points; status=solved only after turn 4
retro.lessons has at least one lesson with known_at
case.json was written only via pas (no hand edits): pas check exits 0 or 4, never 1

baseline_expectation: Without the skill, the model typically lists cards in prose, treats the secured-card preference as a rule, and does not verify issuer requirements. Compare A2, A3, A6, A7.
